messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content: When you throw a ball straight upward, it experiences a constant downward acceleration due to gravity. That acceleration is approximately **–9.8 m/s²** (the negative sign indicates direction opposite to the initial motion). It doesn’t depend on the initial speed; whether you throw it at 5 m/s or any other speed, the acceleration remains about –9.8 m/s² under standard Earth conditions.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They want the acceleration. But acceleration due to gravity is constant ~9.8 m/s^2 downward. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2 (downwards). No need to call function.
